description.narrative: In 2025, the GoU launched the Accelerated Integrated Development of Districts and Cities Program (AIDP) to drive local economic development through targeted infrastructure investments and enhanced service delivery. The AIDP focuses on 16 priority districts and cities selected for their strategic importance to regional growth and inclusion. Implemented within the framework of the country's existing intergovernmental fiscal system, the AIDP channels capital funds to regional governments, which are responsible for financing and executing infrastructure projects in the selected cities/districts. To address the institutional weaknesses and enhance the overall impact of the AIDP, the GoU is partnering with the WB to strengthen its design and implementation, through the Livable and Productive Cities Program (LPCP – the Program). The Program introduces a performance based transfer model, where annual capital grant allocations from the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MoEF) are contingent upon subnational performance. The eligible investments under the Program include but are not limited to connectivity and mobility infrastructure such as urban roads, pedestrian walkways, and bicycle paths; tourism and economic development assets; water supply and sanitation systems; stormwater drainage; social infrastructure such as hospitals, schools, youth and community facilities; refurbishment of municipal assets; preparation of planning documents; digital systems, including municipal spatial data systems; and procurement of municipal vehicles. Investments deemed to carry substantial or high environmental or social risks, as well as those considered temporary or non-strategic, such as gravel roads or temporary relocation facilities, are explicitly excluded from eligibility. The Operation comprises components designed as Program-for-Results (PforR - Program) and Investment Project Financing (IPF - Project). The Program is intended to incentivize better planning, more coordinated investment delivery, and enhanced sustainability of municipal infrastructure and services within the 16 participating cities and districts, the Program will support the introduction of structured, participatory planning processes at the District/City level; the adoption of spatial and area-based strategic plans to guide infrastructure investments in the target districts/cities; and the use of performance-based incentives to promote transparency, improve technical quality, and ensure timely execution of capital municipal infrastructure. The environmental and social risks of the Program are addressed under the Environmental and Social Systems Assessment (ESSA) which is drafted, disclosed and consulted prior to appraisal. To complement the Program component and address capacity constraints at the national level, the Program includes an IPF component, to ensure that subnational activities under the Program are receiving national level institutional support and TA. Managed by the MoEF, the Project complements the Program by providing the upstream TA and capacity-building necessary for effective and consistent implementation across subnational governments through (i) Program Management and Oversight, and (ii) Capacity Building.
To enhance subnational governments capacity for planning and delivery of improved municipal infrastructure and services in participating districts and cities
